chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Atiyyah ibn Rustam, who said:
I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who pronounced zihar from his wife. He said: If it is in the oath, there is no penalty upon him.

key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Zihar (a specific form of divorce in Islamic jurisprudence)
key_terms.فَلَا شَيْءَ: No penalty/expiation (referring to the lack of required kaffarah)
key_terms.يَمِينٍ: Oath (specifically a simple oath, as opposed to a formal declaration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zihar if it is pronounced with a simple oath?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal nuance of *Zihar* by distinguishing between a formal declaration and a simple oath (*yamin*). He rules that if the pronouncement relies solely on a simple oath rather than an explicit, binding declaration, no expiation (*kaffarah*) is due, highlighting the Shia emphasis on precise linguistic intent in marital jurisprudence.
